issues.display_title: Issue #531: Centralize Post Bookmark State Resolution
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Post Bookmark State Resolution

Summary

Added PostFunctions.ResolveBookmarkState and replaced seven duplicated bookmark-state blocks with direct assignments. Existing bookmark and folder response values remain unchanged.

Changes

  • Added ResolveBookmarkState(bookmarks, slug, enabled) (bool, *string) in PostsFunctions.go.
  • Replaced the repeated blocks in six Posts flows and one Search flow.
  • Added TestResolveBookmarkState in PostsFunctions_test.go.

Migrated Flows

  • Posts/DetailPost.go
  • Posts/MostPopularPost.go
  • Posts/NearestPost.go
  • Posts/NearestPostForViewsPanorama.go
  • Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go
  • Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go
  • Search/SearchPost.go

Each flow now assigns both response fields directly:

post.Bookmark, post.Folder = PostFunctions.ResolveBookmarkState(bookmarks, post.Slug, enabled)

Behavior Compatibility

The helper preserves the previous branches:

  • Disabled checks return false, nil without reading the bookmark map.
  • Missing slugs and non-map values return false, nil.
  • A valid bookmark map returns true.
  • A string folder is returned by pointer; an absent or non-string folder remains nil.

No response field, response type, Redis key, query, or endpoint condition was changed.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused test was added before the helper and initially failed because ResolveBookmarkState was undefined. After the minimum helper was added, it passed for disabled, invalid, folderless, and saved bookmark states.

Scope Audit

  • 7 helper calls across 7 Action files.
  • 0 direct .Bookmark = true assignments remain outside Slim and Worker files.
  • 7 Action files and 2 PostFunctions files changed.
  • No Slim or Worker file changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l <changed Go files>
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • The focused bookmark-state test passes.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Seven post response flows repeated the same bookmark-state assignment:

post.Bookmark = false
post.Folder = nil
if checkBookmark {
	if bookmark, ok := bookmarks[post.Slug].(map[string]interface{}); ok {
		post.Bookmark = true
		if folder, ok := bookmark["folder"].(string); ok {
			post.Folder = &folder
		}
	}
}

The nested block was duplicated across related Posts and Search flows, making the same response behavior harder to maintain consistently.

Scope

  • Add one shared PostFunctions.ResolveBookmarkState helper.
  • Replace the matching bookmark-state blocks in six Posts files and SearchPost.go.
  • Add a focused test for enabled, disabled, invalid, and folderless bookmark states.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • bookmark = false and folder = nil when bookmark checks are disabled.
  • bookmark = false and folder = nil when the slug is absent or its value is not a bookmark map.
  • bookmark = true when a bookmark map exists, even if its folder is absent.
  • A non-nil folder containing the existing folder string when available.
  • Every existing response field, type, and assignment target.

Out of Scope

  • Changing Redis.ListBookmarksUser or its stored data shape.
  • Changing when each endpoint enables bookmark checks.
  • Changing response models or mobile-facing response schemas.
  • Updating Slim or Worker files.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One helper owns bookmark and folder resolution.
  • All seven matching non-Slim/Worker flows use the helper.
  • No matching direct bookmark-state block remains outside Slim and Worker files.
  • A focused test verifies all existing result branches.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-03. No commit was created.

Implementation: Centralize Place Contributor Resolution

Summary

Added a local resolvePlaceContributors helper and replaced the two duplicated contributor-processing blocks in GetPlaceList.go. Both filtered and default Place List responses now use the same transformation without changing their response fields or values.

Changes

  • Added resolvePlaceContributors(raw json.RawMessage) ([]Models.PlaceContributor, int).
  • Replaced contributor processing in the include response branch.
  • Replaced contributor processing in the default response branch.
  • Added focused tests in GetPlaceList_test.go.

Both response branches now use:

contributors, overflow := resolvePlaceContributors(p.Contributors.RawMessage)

Behavior Compatibility

The helper preserves the previous operation order:

  1. Decode a nested contributor array and flatten it when valid.
  2. Otherwise, decode a single-level contributor array.
  3. Discard the single-level result when decoding returns an error.
  4. Remove empty and duplicate usernames while preserving the first occurrence.
  5. Return the first four unique contributors and calculate the remainder as overflow.

Empty or invalid input still produces an empty non-nil contributor slice and zero overflow. No query, model, response key, response type, or endpoint condition changed.

Test-Driven Verification

The initial helper tests failed because resolvePlaceContributors did not exist. After extraction, nested, single-level, empty, deduplication, ordering, limit, and overflow cases passed.

A malformed mixed-type test then demonstrated that assigning directly into the result slice could retain partially decoded data. The fallback was changed to match the previous implementation: assign the single-level slice only when json.Unmarshal succeeds. The regression test then passed.

Scope Audit

  • 1 local helper added.
  • 2 duplicated blocks replaced.
  • 1 production file and 1 test file changed.
  • No response model or schema changed.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated file changed.
  • Existing unrelated working-tree changes were not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList.go src/Action/V1/Places/GetPlaceList_test.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • Changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Place tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

GetPlaceList.go repeated the same contributor-processing block in its filtered and default response branches. Both blocks decoded contributor JSON, flattened nested arrays, removed duplicate usernames, limited the result to four contributors, and calculated overflow.

Keeping both copies allowed the two response paths to drift even though they require identical contributor data.

Scope

  • Add one local resolvePlaceContributors helper in GetPlaceList.go.
  • Replace both matching contributor-processing blocks with the helper.
  • Add focused tests for nested, single-level, empty, duplicate, overflow, and invalid contributor data.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Support for nested and single-level contributor arrays.
  • Original contributor ordering.
  • Deduplication by username, keeping the first occurrence.
  • Exclusion of empty usernames.
  • A maximum of four returned contributors.
  • Overflow as the number of unique contributors beyond four.
  • An empty non-nil contributor slice when no valid data exists.
  • Rejection of partially decoded single-level data when JSON decoding returns an error.
  • Every existing response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Changing place queries, sorting, pagination, or filtering.
  • Changing the PlaceContributor or PlaceListItemResponse models.
  • Changing response keys or mobile-facing response schemas.
  • Moving the helper into a global utility package; the logic is specific to Place List responses.
  • Updating other Places, Slim, Worker, or Support flows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One helper owns the duplicated contributor processing.
  • Both Place List response branches use the helper.
  • No duplicate contributor-processing block remains in GetPlaceList.go.
  • Focused tests cover all preserved input shapes and edge cases.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-04. No commit was created.

issues.display_title: Issue #533: Centralize Broadcast Post Data Construction
issues.main_description_html:
Implementation: Centralize Broadcast Post Data Construction

Summary

Added the package-local buildBroadcastPostData helper and replaced the duplicated post-data construction in both Broadcast list flows. The helper preserves the existing post, user, optional JSON, and error behavior.

Changes

  • Added BroadcastFunctions.go containing buildBroadcastPostData.
  • Updated ListBroadcast.go to use the helper.
  • Updated ListPotdBroadcast.go to use the helper while retaining its existing include checks.
  • Added BroadcastFunctions_test.go for response shape and decode failures.

Both callers now use:

post, user, err := buildBroadcastPostData(broadcast)
if err != nil {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, err.Error())
}

Response Compatibility

The helper still decodes fields in the previous order:

  1. panorama_quality
  2. animation_filter
  3. little_planet_filter

It then builds the same post fields:

  • slug_post
  • panorama_preview
  • post_type
  • thumbnail
  • animation
  • animation_filter
  • little_planet
  • little_planet_filter
  • panorama_quality
  • pending

The user map still contains avatar, fullname, and username. Decode failures retain their previous status and message. No response key, type, query, or endpoint condition changed.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused tests were added before the helper and initially failed because buildBroadcastPostData was undefined. After the minimum helper and caller replacements were added, the tests passed for the complete post/user mapping and each existing JSON decode error.

Scope Audit

  • 1 package-local helper added.
  • 2 duplicated blocks replaced across 2 Broadcast files.
  • 62 duplicated caller lines removed.
  • No bookmark construction, response model, or schema changed.
  • No Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated file changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Broadcast/BroadcastFunctions.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/BroadcastFunctions_test.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListBroadcast.go src/Action/V1/Broadcast/ListPotdBroadcast.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Broadcast tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

ListBroadcast.go and ListPotdBroadcast.go repeated the same post-data construction. Both flows decoded three optional JSON fields and built identical post and user response maps.

The duplicate blocks made the two related Broadcast responses vulnerable to field or error-handling drift.

Scope

  • Add one package-local buildBroadcastPostData helper.
  • Replace the matching blocks in ListBroadcast.go and ListPotdBroadcast.go.
  • Add focused tests for response mapping and existing decode errors.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • Decoding of panorama_quality, animation_filter, and little_planet_filter through Functions.DecodeOptionalJSONMap.
  • Existing nil handling for optional JSON fields.
  • Every field and value in the post response map.
  • Every field and value in the user response map.
  • Decode order and existing error messages.
  • Each endpoint's current include behavior and response structure.

Out of Scope

  • Changing Broadcast queries, filters, sorting, or pagination.
  • Centralizing bookmark response construction.
  • Changing response models or mobile-facing response schemas.
  • Changing the POTD include rules.
  • Updating Slim, Worker, Support, or unrelated flows.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One helper owns the shared Broadcast post and user mapping.
  • Both matching Broadcast flows use the helper.
  • No matching decode-and-map block remains in either caller.
  • Focused tests cover successful mapping and all three decode errors.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Implementation: Centralize Timeline Post Enrichment

Summary

Added package-local timeline post enrichment helpers and replaced the duplicated loops in three post-list flows. Elasticsearch counters, description processing, bookmark state, folder state, errors, and response schemas remain unchanged.

Changes

  • Added PostResponse.go containing enrichTimelinePosts and applyTimelinePostData.
  • Updated MostPopularPost.go.
  • Updated TimeLinePostJustForYou.go.
  • Updated TimeLinePostRecent.go.
  • Added focused tests in PostResponse_test.go.

Each caller now uses:

if err := enrichTimelinePosts(c, postsTimeline, listBookmarks, checkBookmark); err != nil {
	return Functions.ErrorResponse(c, 500, fiber.ErrInternalServerError.Message, "Failed to get data Elastic")
}

Behavior Compatibility

For each post, enrichTimelinePosts still:

  1. Retrieves counters from post_<prefix> using document ID post_<slug>.
  2. Stops on the first retrieval error.
  3. Replaces a missing or empty counter map with the same three zero-valued counters.
  4. Processes a non-empty description through PostFunctions.UnescapeAndWrapText.
  5. Resolves bookmark and folder through PostFunctions.ResolveBookmarkState.

The helper iterates the original slice in place and in the original order. An empty slice remains a no-op. No query, error response, response field, or response type changed.

Test-Driven Verification

The focused tests were added before the helpers and initially failed because applyTimelinePostData and enrichTimelinePosts were undefined. After the minimum implementation was added, the tests passed for:

  • Default zero-valued counters.
  • Preservation of existing counter data.
  • Existing description transformation.
  • Bookmark and folder assignment.
  • Disabled bookmark handling.
  • Empty post lists.

Scope Audit

  • 2 package-local helpers added.
  • 3 duplicated enrichment loops replaced.
  • 101 duplicated lines removed from the three callers.
  • No DetailPost, NearestPost, Search, Slim, Worker, or Support flow changed.
  • No response model or schema changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

gofmt -l src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse.go src/Action/V1/Posts/PostResponse_test.go src/Action/V1/Posts/MostPopularPost.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostJustForYou.go src/Action/V1/Posts/TimeLinePostRecent.go
go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • Focused Posts tests pass.
  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Three related post-list flows repeated the same enrichment loop for every Models.V1DetailPost:

  • Retrieve post counters from Elasticsearch.
  • Supply zero-valued counters when no counter document exists.
  • Unescape and wrap the description.
  • Resolve bookmark and folder state.

The duplicated loops made their response behavior harder to maintain consistently.

Scope

  • Add package-local timeline post enrichment helpers.
  • Replace the matching loops in MostPopularPost.go, TimeLinePostJustForYou.go, and TimeLinePostRecent.go.
  • Add focused tests for the existing counter, description, bookmark, folder, and empty-list behavior.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • One sequential Elasticsearch lookup per returned post.
  • Elasticsearch index post_<prefix> and document ID post_<slug>.
  • Immediate failure when any Elasticsearch lookup fails.
  • The existing Failed to get data Elastic response from each caller.
  • Default counter_view, counter_like, and counter_comment values of zero.
  • Existing non-empty counter data without modification.
  • Existing description, short-description, and long-description values.
  • Existing bookmark and folder resolution.
  • Post ordering and every response field and type.

Out of Scope

  • Changing post queries, filters, sorting, or pagination.
  • Batching or parallelizing Elasticsearch requests.
  • Updating DetailPost, NearestPost, Search, Slim, Worker, or Support flows.
  • Changing response models or mobile-facing response schemas.

Acceptance Criteria

  • One shared loop owns the matching timeline post enrichment.
  • All three matching callers use the helper.
  • No matching enrichment loop remains in those callers.
  • Focused tests lock the existing transformation behavior.
  • All changed Go files are formatted.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Implementation: Batch Followed User Lookup

Summary

Added one shared followed-user batch lookup and applied it to five related user-list flows. Each flow now collects the current page's user IDs, performs at most one followers query, then reads followed values from a map while building the unchanged response.

Changes

  • Added UserFunctions.GetFollowedUserIDs in UsersFunctions.go.
  • Added the internal followedUserIDSet map builder.
  • Updated SearchUser.go.
  • Updated ProfileFollower.go.
  • Updated ProfileFollowing.go.
  • Updated SearchProfileFollower.go.
  • Updated SearchProfileFollowing.go.
  • Added UsersFunctions_test.go.
  • Added a comment in every caller explaining why IDs are collected before response construction.

The helper performs the equivalent of:

SELECT user_id
FROM followers
WHERE follower_id = :current_user_id
  AND user_id IN (:candidate_user_ids);

Returned IDs become a lookup map:

followedUserIDs[userID]

Go map lookup returns false when the user ID is absent, matching the previous default value.

Why Two Loops

The first in-memory loop extracts candidate IDs from the page result. The batch query must run after those IDs are known. The second loop builds or enriches the response using the completed lookup map.

The two O(N) memory loops replace N database round trips. Default page sizes are small, while avoiding repeated database queries removes the expensive part of the old flow.

Behavior Compatibility

  • The batch query uses the same relationship direction as the old checks: follower_id is the current user and user_id is the candidate user.
  • Viewer flows skip the helper and retain followed: false.
  • Empty candidate lists return an empty map without querying the database.
  • User ordering, pagination, filtering, hide, encryption, and response fields are unchanged.
  • SearchUser and ProfileFollower still panic on followed-query errors, matching their previous use of CheckFollowed.
  • ProfileFollowing, SearchProfileFollower, and SearchProfileFollowing still return the existing HTTP 500 response on followed-query errors.
  • The per-user posts query in SearchUser remains unchanged.

Test-Driven Verification

TestFollowedUserIDSet was added first and failed because followedUserIDSet did not exist. After implementation, the test verifies:

  • Returned user IDs resolve to true.
  • Missing user IDs resolve to false.
  • Duplicate IDs do not affect the result.

Scope Audit

  • 1 reusable batch query helper added.
  • 1 small internal map builder added.
  • 5 N+1 followed-status loops replaced.
  • CheckFollowed and unrelated callers remain unchanged.
  • No API response model or mobile-facing schema changed.
  • The existing API collection environment edit was not modified.

Verification

go test -count=1 ./...
go vet ./...
git diff --check

Results:

  • The complete Go test suite passes with no failing package.
  • go vet ./... succeeds.
  • git diff --check succeeds.

Problem

Five related user-list flows checked followed status with one database query for every returned user:

  • SearchUser.go
  • ProfileFollower.go
  • ProfileFollowing.go
  • SearchProfileFollower.go
  • SearchProfileFollowing.go

This caused an N+1 query pattern. A page containing N users required N additional queries against followers only to populate the existing followed field.

Scope

  • Add a reusable followed-user batch lookup under UserFunctions.
  • Collect candidate user IDs from each result page.
  • Retrieve all matching followed user IDs with one query.
  • Resolve each existing followed value through an in-memory lookup.
  • Add a focused test for followed-ID set construction.
  • Document why ID collection and response construction use separate loops.

Behavior Boundary

The refactor must preserve:

  • The meaning and boolean type of followed.
  • Existing response fields and nesting.
  • User ordering, filters, pagination, and limits.
  • Existing hide behavior in follower and following responses.
  • Viewer responses with followed: false and no followed-status query.
  • Empty result behavior.
  • Existing encrypted and unencrypted response structures.
  • Existing database error behavior: panic in SearchUser and ProfileFollower, HTTP 500 in the other three flows.

Out of Scope

  • Changing CheckFollowed or its remaining callers.
  • Refactoring per-user post retrieval in SearchUser.
  • Updating Likes, Slim, Worker, or Support flows.
  • Adding joins to the main user queries.
  • Changing mobile-facing response schemas or values.

Acceptance Criteria

  • GetFollowedUserIDs retrieves followed status for all candidate IDs with at most one query.
  • All five scoped flows use the batch helper.
  • No scoped flow queries followed status inside its response loop.
  • Missing IDs resolve to false; returned IDs resolve to true.
  • Existing failure behavior remains unchanged per caller.
  • A code comment explains the two-loop tradeoff.
  • go test -count=1 ./... passes.
  • go vet ./... passes.
  • git diff --check passes.

Delivery

Implemented in the working tree on 2026-09-04. No commit was created.
